A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COREL research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched across the revised layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments on METR-LA, CER-E and AQI, GPVAR simulations, adaptation results and interval-width optimization experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments across those datasets and reports revised results, additional GPVAR interval widths, runtime measurements and learned-graph analysis.

M1.justification: COREL retains its spatiotemporal quantile network, sparse graph learning, pinball objective, interval construction and node-embedding adaptation. Per-series notation and expanded implementation explanations do not establish a changed COREL procedure; alternative graph distributions are discussed prospectively.

E1.justification: Both versions use METR-LA traffic, CER-E electricity consumption, AQI pollution measurements and the same GPVAR simulation. Forecasting tasks and the CER-E adaptation scenario remain unchanged; the new graph analysis uses the existing GPVAR experiment.

E2.justification: The comparator roster is retained, and SCPI is corrected to SPCI rather than replaced. However, CORNN's reported specification changes: v1 removes only message-passing layers, whereas v2 also removes node embeddings and allows multiple GRU layers (Section 5.1 and Appendix D).

E3.justification: Appendix F changes CORNN's stated hyperparameter search from matching COREL's to additionally tuning GRU depth. Appendix E adds a factor of 100 to the coverage-gap formula, matching the percentage scale already used in v1's tables. Main splits, forecasting horizons and training budgets remain; newly disclosed early-stopping and adaptation settings do not establish changes to those procedures.

E4.justification: New Appendix G.1 and Figure 2 examine recovery of the GPVAR graph, showing true edges alongside additional learned links. The revised CORNN control also changes the component ablation. The existing adaptation and quantile-offset analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report results with ± values, without specifying run counts, seeds or what those uncertainty values represent. v2 adds no statistical testing or uncertainty-estimation procedure; changed values and additional result entries retain the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Numerical results are extensively replaced in Table 1, the adaptation table (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 3), and Table 4. For example, the reported METR-LA/RNN COREL Winkler score changes from 25.55 to 23.78, although the overall leading-method pattern remains. v2 also adds GPVAR interval widths and METR-LA training/testing times. These are revised and newly reported results, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.1 and Appendix A replace the vector-valued coverage event with coverage for an individual series, correcting the scope of the guarantee while retaining the total-variation argument. Equations 3-4 correct the forecast target to t+H. Section 3.3 also adds an O(WN+E) forward-pass scaling statement for a standard TTS architecture.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: graph-based conformal prediction for correlated series, learned relationships without a supplied graph, compatibility with pretrained predictors, local adaptation and competitive uncertainty estimates. Additional evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes separate prediction intervals from modeling the joint distribution and expands discussion of scalability and nonstationary coverage guarantees. It relates GPVAR widths to the theoretical optimum and explains that exact graph recovery is unnecessary. Appendix G.2 now acknowledges reduced coverage from width optimization instead of describing coverage as approximately retained.

D1.justification: Appendices B-F replace a future code-release promise with reported repository availability and fill substantial reproducibility gaps. Added details include the base-model early-stopping split, GPVAR noise and model dimensions, message-passing reference, and adaptation architecture, learning rate and fine-tuning budget. Hardware-specific training/testing times are also supplied. These are largely disclosures about retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Feldman et al. on multiple-output quantile regression, Lee et al. (2025) on weighted time-series CP, Zhao et al. on link prediction, Chiang et al. on scalable GNNs, and Satorras et al. for implementation context. These extend the discussion without substantially changing the novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The section sequence and most prose remain recognizable. v2 corrects wording and terminology, adds explanatory subheadings, reorganizes Appendix G into two subsections, expands the limitations paragraph, and adds impact and acknowledgment sections. These are localized edits rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds the paired adjacency-matrix display in Figure 2 and PI-Width columns to the GPVAR table. The GPVAR and adaptation tables exchange numbering and placement. Conference styling changes headers, typography and captions, while Figure 1 and the main two-column/single-column-appendix layout are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through reported code availability and concrete experimental settings, and states the coverage guarantee and limitations more precisely. The graph analysis and GPVAR interval widths add useful support. These gains are limited: the revised CORNN ablation changes both message passing and embeddings, making attribution specifically to graph processing less clean, and revised scores alone do not demonstrate better methodology.
